title: Sacred Falgu River — History, Curse of Sita & Spiritual Significance for Pind Daan
metaDescription: Discover the divine history of Gaya's Falgu River, the story of Sita's curse, why the river flows underground, and its central role in ancestral Pind Daan & Tarpan rites.
author: Acharya Pandit V. K. Gayawal
summary: The Falgu River carries one of Hinduism's most poignant stories — the curse of Goddess Sita — explaining why its waters flow invisibly beneath the sand. Pilgrims perform Tarpan and Pinda offerings on its holy banks.
content:
The Falgu (also spelled Phalgu) River flows through the sacred city of Gaya in Bihar, India. Unlike other rivers visible on the surface, the Falgu is a unique river that flows primarily beneath a sandy riverbed, with water visible only in certain seasons and at specific sacred ghats.

### The Legend of Sita's Curse
According to Valmiki Ramayana tradition, when Lord Rama went into the forest to collect flowers and Brahmin ingredients for King Dasharatha's Pinda ceremony, Goddess Sita — alone on the riverbank — saw a vision of her departed father-in-law appearing and asking for immediate ancestral offerings. Unable to wait for Rama, Sita performed the Pinda ceremony using sand, the Falgu River, an Akshayvat leaf, and a cow as witnesses.

When Rama returned, the Falgu River denied being a witness to Sita's ceremony. Enraged by this untruth, Goddess Sita cursed the Falgu River to flow underground and invisibly forever — which is why even today the river flows as an antarvahini (underground river).

### The Spiritual Significance for Pilgrims
Despite flowing underground, the Falgu River retains immense sanctity. Pilgrims descend to Vishnupad Ghat and Sitakund Ghat to perform:
- **Pinda Visarjan**: Immersion of rice Pindas into the sacred sand
- **Tarpan**: Water offering with sesame seeds for departed ancestors
- **Holy Dip**: Ritual bathing before temple entry

sections.heading: Vishnupad Ghat on the Falgu River
sections.body: The primary ghat where most pilgrims perform their Pinda and Tarpan ceremonies, directly adjacent to the Vishnupad Temple complex. Gayawal Purohits guide each family through the Sankalp (ritual vow) before proceedings begin.

sections.heading: Best Time to Visit Falgu River
sections.body: While Pind Daan can be performed throughout the year at Falgu Ghat, the most spiritually potent period is during Pitru Paksha (16 days before Sharad Navratri). During monsoon season (July-September), seasonal water may be visible in the river channel.

faqs.question: Why does the Falgu River flow underground?
faqs.answer: According to sacred legend, Goddess Sita cursed the Falgu River for bearing false witness when she performed ancestral rites for King Dasharatha during Rama's absence.

faqs.question: Can Pind Daan be performed at the Falgu River directly?
faqs.answer: Yes. Falgu Ghat is one of the primary locations for Pinda Visarjan and Tarpan, guided by your assigned Gayawal Purohit.

sources: Archaeological Survey of India — Gaya District
